strategy.summary: Reproduce PR #9835 by building statsmodels from the buggy commit 383d9707516a and running the developer's new test_vif_instability in statsmodels/stats/tests/test_influence.py. On the buggy revision variance_inflation_factor has no standardize keyword, so the test fails at its first call with TypeError; on the fixed revision the keyword exists and all three assertion blocks should pass. The transition as written is driven mainly by the missing keyword, so the numerical content of the test is only partly exercised by the buggy-revision failure.

system_packages: C and Fortran compilers usable by the build backend (gcc/gfortran or equivalent)
build_commands: python -m pip install -e . --no-build-isolation  (or python -m pip install -e . after installing the build requirements from pyproject.toml)
pinned_because: numpy kept at or below 2.3: era ceiling from the evidence, numerically relevant but not a documented constraint, so this is an era-inferred pin and not a documented one
python version not stated by the evidence; choose a Python supported by the chosen numpy and scipy and record it in the run log
statsmodels itself is unbounded in the evidence: the strategy builds the exact buggy commit rather than relying on a released version

strategy.reproducing_test: statsmodels/stats/tests/test_influence.py::test_vif_instability (new in the PR); also statsmodels/stats/tests/test_outliers_influence.py::test_reset_stata, which the PR modifies to pass standardize=False
strategy.success_criterion: On buggy 383d9707516a: test_vif_instability fails (TypeError on the standardize keyword at the first variance_inflation_factor call; test_reset_stata also fails with TypeError on the same keyword). On the fixed revision: both tests pass, with the standardize=True call emitting no UserWarning, the standardize=False call on the ill-conditioned matrix emitting the 'The design matrix is poorly conditioned' UserWarning and returning a value greater than 100, and the clean-data standardize=True and standardize=False results agreeing at rtol=1e-7.
strategy.numerical_probe: Call variance_inflation_factor on the test's exog (seed 42, n=500, columns ones, log(x1), 1/x2, x1, x2) with standardize=False and standardize=True and inspect whether the legacy path warns and explodes while the standardized path does not.

input_output_examples.input: variance_inflation_factor(exog, 0, standardize=True) on the test's ill-conditioned exog
input_output_examples.buggy_output: TypeError: variance_inflation_factor() got an unexpected keyword argument 'standardize'
input_output_examples.expected_output: returns a finite float without raising; the assertion assert_allclose(vif_const, 1.0, atol=1e-2) is then evaluated

input_output_examples.input: variance_inflation_factor(exog, 0, standardize=False) inside pytest.warns(UserWarning, match='The design matrix is poorly conditioned')
input_output_examples.buggy_output: TypeError on the standardize keyword; no 'poorly conditioned' warning is ever emitted
input_output_examples.expected_output: UserWarning matching 'The design matrix is poorly conditioned' is emitted and the returned value is greater than 100

risks: On the buggy revision the test fails at the first keyword call with TypeError, so the transition is decided by the signature change rather than by numerics; a numerically-motivated check requires running the buggy code with the keyword removed or patched, which is not the developer's test.

The fixed-revision pass depends on the 'poorly conditioned' warning text and on the exact r_squared clipping threshold; the evidence does not give the threshold, so a small change in conditioning could move the outcome.

The clean-data block uses np.random.normal after np.random.seed(42) inside the same test, so it is deterministic in the test as written; the evidence's statement that it has no seed is incomplete, and this strategy relies on the seed set at the top of the function.
The exog dtype is not stated by the evidence; the test builds float64 arrays via np.column_stack of float results, so float64 is assumed.

The 'ones' column VIF is asserted against 1.0 with atol=1e-2; this is the test's own expectation and is not derived from the passages, and may depend on the exact standardization and centering in the fix.

The defect is described in the evidence as platform-independent, but the floating-point cancellation in 1-rsquared is sensitive to BLAS and libm implementation; results may differ across x86 and ARM builds, so the transition is not guaranteed on other platforms.
Sanitisers are not indicated by the evidence and are not needed here; no architecture-specific behaviour is stated.

oracle.tolerance: rtol=1e-7 for standardize=True vs standardize=False on clean data; atol=1e-2 for the constant-column VIF against 1.0; the warning-match regex for the ill-conditioned legacy path
oracle.reference_source: the developer's test diff in PR #9835 (test_vif_instability and the adjusted test_reset_stata)
oracle.why: The test asserts agreement between the two standardize settings on clean data and a warning plus large value on the legacy path; these are the pass/fail criteria the transition depends on.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: The first call variance_inflation_factor(exog, 0, standardize=True) raises TypeError because the buggy signature has no standardize keyword, so test_vif_instability fails before any numerical assertion runs; test_reset_stata fails the same way on its standardize=False call.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: With the keyword present: the standardize=True call on the ill-conditioned matrix emits no UserWarning and returns a value satisfying the atol=1e-2 check; the standardize=False call emits the 'poorly conditioned' UserWarning and returns a value greater than 100; the clean-data standardize=True and standardize=False results agree at rtol=1e-7; test_reset_stata returns 16.4394 to four decimals on both array and DataFrame inputs.
